<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Make process checkpoint/restore (CRIU plus `cuda-checkpoint`, run by an external orchestrator such as [ai-dynamo/snapshot](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/snapshot)) a first-class engine lifecycle with a production HTTP surface: `POST /checkpoint/prepare`, `GET /checkpoint/status`, `POST /checkpoint/restore`, and `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`, in the Python and Rust frontends. Implements the minimal API from RFC #60422 ([summary](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/60422#issuecomment-6187366614)), building on the communicator hooks from #46877 and the paused-request rejection from #51488.

## Claims

- The engine owns a repeatable lifecycle: `running → preparing → prepared → restoring → running`, or `failed`. `AsyncLLM.checkpoint_prepare(mode)` and `checkpoint_restore()` each run as one engine call, so repeated and concurrent calls (several API servers, DP) are no-ops. `checkpoint_state()` reports the state; DP engines merge as failed if any failed, otherwise the shared state.
- `POST /checkpoint/prepare?mode=wait|abort|keep` drains with the pause mode, discards the KV cache and runs the workers' `checkpoint_prepare` hooks. It returns 200 once started (poll status), or 400 with the reason if the engine cannot prepare now, like the other admin routes (for example asleep or mid-cycle).
- `GET /checkpoint/status` returns 200 when prepared, 503 until then and 500 after a failure. `POST /checkpoint/restore` returns 200 when restoring or done (orchestrators redeliver), 400 while preparing or failed. Both work after a restore or in place.
- While an engine does not serve, new requests get the retryable `engine_paused` error from #51488, and `sleep`, `wake_up` and `resume_scheduler` are refused. `/health` keeps its upstream meaning and returns 200, as for a sleeping engine.
- `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` prepares each engine once it starts, for capture-at-startup orchestrators.
- The routes exist only with `--enable-sleep-mode`, which preparing requires, as the fault-tolerance and profiler routes exist only with their flags. They document their status codes in the OpenAPI schema.
- The Rust frontend serves the same three routes with the same status codes, bodies and sleep-mode gating.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run` on the changed files (ruff, mypy, typos, markdownlint, SPDX, config docstrings) passes.
- New unit tests in `tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py`:
  - `test_checkpoint_prepare_then_restore_run_in_order`: preparing releases the KV cache before the worker hooks, restoring runs the hooks before the KV cache wakes and scheduling resumes, repeats are no-ops, and new requests are rejected in between.
  - `test_checkpoint_prepare_fails_on_drain_barrier_error`: a failing device sync at the end of the drain leaves the engine `failed` and still rejecting, for both an immediate and a deferred drain.
- End to end with ai-dynamo/snapshot (CRIU plus `cuda-checkpoint`) on 8x B200, using an earlier revision of this lifecycle with the same status route, the restore route under its earlier name `/checkpoint/resume`, and `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup`, restoring into a new pod:

  | Configuration | Result |
  | :-- | :-- |
  | Qwen3-30B-A3B DEP8, Python frontend | Source status 200 `prepared`. After restore and `/checkpoint/resume`: a repeated call 200, correct greedy completions, 16/16 concurrent requests. |
  | Same, Rust frontend | Same results. |
  | P/D over NIXL, prefill and decode restored on different nodes, then a second prefill from the same checkpoint (stacked follow-up) | 3/3 greedy matches per phase, 0 failed transfers, two concurrent empty resumes both 200. |

- The first revision of this PR on 1x B200 (`vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --enable-sleep-mode`, Python frontend), two prepare/restore cycles in one process with no capture, when the restore route was `/checkpoint/resume`. `/health` results are left out of both tables because those runs returned 503 while not serving, which this PR no longer does:

  | Step | Result |
  | :-- | :-- |
  | Serving | status 503 `running`, completion `" Paris. The capital of France is also the capital of the"` |
  | `POST /checkpoint/prepare` | 200 `prepared` (idle server), status 200, a completion gets 503 `Generation is paused. Please retry after it resumes.` |
  | Repeated prepare | 200 `prepared` |
  | `POST /sleep` (dev mode) mid-cycle | refused: `Cannot sleep while the checkpoint state is prepared` |
  | Two concurrent `POST /checkpoint/resume` (now `/checkpoint/restore`) | both 200 `running`; status 503 `running`, same completion as before |

- `pytest tests/v1/engine/test_engine_core.py -k "checkpoint or pause or kv_cache_release or wake_up or reject"`: 22 passed on this branch.
- Existing route-level tests cover the Python routes: the `test_openai_schema.py` fuzz test (the test server has no sleep mode, so the routes are absent) and the `test_authentication_middleware.py` route discovery, whose mock model config now enables sleep mode so the routes are checked as unauthenticated. Buildkite [#97267](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/97267) passed all 357 jobs before the Rust routes were added.
- Rust frontend: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -D warnings`, and the `vllm-server` and `vllm-engine-core-client` tests pass (Rust 1.95). No new Rust tests: CI's Rust frontend coverage reruns existing Python end-to-end tests, and none of them exercise these routes. The Rust routes were validated end to end with Snapshot in the table above.



## Details

**Why this shape.** The pieces exist upstream, but an external orchestrator cannot use them safely: `/pause`, `/sleep` and `/wake_up` are dev-mode routes, `checkpoint_prepare/restore` (#46877) only run the worker hooks and leave sequencing to the caller, nothing reports where the engine is, and other calls can interleave. Moving each step into one engine call gives an idempotent, observable contract that any orchestrator (Snapshot, scripts, future live migration) can drive over HTTP, and that the Rust frontend can call without copying the sequence.

`AsyncLLM.checkpoint_prepare()` and `checkpoint_restore()` previously only ran the worker communicator hooks, and callers paused and slept first. They now run the whole step and refuse an engine that is already asleep. The worker-level hooks are unchanged.

**Not duplicate.** #51360 (`vllm snapshot`), #52132, #35934, #37921, #58183 and #61544 implement checkpointing inside vLLM (CRIU and/or `cuda-checkpoint`). This PR adds no checkpointing code; it is the boundary an external orchestrator needs, and those paths could reuse the same lifecycle later. #48311 owns pause/drain/sleep for RL; this PR reuses `pause_generation` and adds no new pause semantics.

**Tradeoffs and limitations.**
- `/health` stays a liveness check, which the multi-port DP supervisor, elastic EP and the documented Kubernetes probes rely on. A prepared engine therefore stays in rotation, and new requests get the retryable `engine_paused` error until it resumes. A readiness signal that stays false until the engine serves can be added later without changing `/health`.
- With `--enable-sleep-mode`, the routes need no API key, like `/scale_elastic_ep` and the dev-mode `/sleep` and `/pause`. They are listed in `docs/usage/security.md`. A deployment that does not want them can block the paths at the proxy.
- `EngineCoreProc.resume_scheduler` now clears `reject_new_requests` after the base class's checks, so a refused resume keeps rejecting requests.
- With data parallelism, the Rust frontend reports a prepare refusal from any engine, and Python reports engine 0's. Engines that accepted keep preparing. Refusal causes are normally the same on every engine.
- Follow-ups, already prototyped: a checkpoint resource registry for CPU offload and HiSparse host memory (galletas1712/vllm#5), and independent P/D restore over NIXL (galletas1712/vllm#3). No gRPC `Control` methods yet.

the multi-port DP supervisor treats a 503 here as a failed child and shuts down all children. can we keep checkpoint preparation from triggering that?
check_health() deliberately succeeds for retired elastic-EP ranks, but this RPC then hits their exited engine and turns the intended 200 into a 500. can we preserve that case?

Right, the extra RPC broke the retired-rank case. Same fix in 9c6b815da1: `/health` is back to upstream, so retired elastic-EP ranks get 200 again and `/health` makes no checkpoint call.

self._checkpoint_state is only set in __init__, so the pre-existing test test_scheduler.py::test_kv_cache_release_after_keep_pause_preserves_requests, which builds EngineCore via object.__new__, now fails with AttributeError on this line.

 - `/scale_elastic_ep` - Trigger scaling operations
 - `/is_scaling_elastic_ep` - Check if scaling is in progress
 
+## Process Checkpoint APIs
+
+For external checkpoint/restore orchestrators, available with `--enable-sleep-mode`. Preparing drains the engine and releases its KV cache and other external state, any number of times. Until `/checkpoint/restore`, new requests get a retryable error and `/health` still returns 200, as while asleep. `--checkpoint-prepare-on-startup` prepares each engine once it starts.
+
+- `/checkpoint/prepare` - Start preparing, draining with `?mode=wait` (default), `abort` or `keep`; 200 once started or already preparing, 400 if the engine cannot prepare now
+- `/checkpoint/status` - Return the state: 200 once prepared, 503 until then, 500 after a failure
+- `/checkpoint/restore` - Bring back released state and serve; 200 if already restoring or serving, 400 while preparing or after a failure
+

 When using the flag VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE=1, you enable development endpoints.

+def _executor_calls(core: EngineCoreProc) -> list[str]:
+    """Executor calls in order, naming collective RPCs by their method."""
+    return [
+        args[0] if name == "collective_rpc" else name
+        for name, args, _ in core.model_executor.mock_calls
+    ]
+
+
+def test_checkpoint_prepare_then_restore_run_in_order():
+    """Preparing drains, then discards the KV cache and releases external
+    state. Restoring brings external state back before the KV cache wakes and
+    scheduling resumes. Repeating either is a no-op."""
+    core = _pausable_engine_core_proc()
+    core.vllm_config = MagicMock()
+    core.model_executor.is_sleeping = False
+    core._reset_caches = MagicMock()
+    core.reject_new_requests = False
+    core.scheduler.get_kv_connector.return_value = None
+
+    assert core.checkpoint_prepare("wait") is None
+    assert core.checkpoint_prepare("wait") is None
+    assert core.checkpoint_state() == (CheckpointState.PREPARED, None)
+    assert core.reject_new_requests
+    assert _executor_calls(core) == [
+        "synchronize_device",
+        "discard",
+        "checkpoint_prepare",
+        "synchronize_device",
+    ]
+
+    core.model_executor.reset_mock()
+    core.checkpoint_restore()
+    core.checkpoint_restore()
+    assert core.checkpoint_state() == (CheckpointState.RUNNING, None)
+    assert _executor_calls(core) == ["checkpoint_restore", "wake_up"]
+    core.scheduler.set_pause_state.assert_called_with(PauseState.UNPAUSED)
+    assert not core.reject_new_requests
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("deferred", [False, True])
+def test_checkpoint_prepare_fails_on_drain_barrier_error(deferred: bool):
+    """A failing barrier at the end of the drain leaves the engine FAILED and
+    still rejecting, whether the drain completes at once or later."""
+    core = _pausable_engine_core_proc()
+    core.vllm_config = MagicMock()
+    core.model_executor.is_sleeping = False
+    core.model_executor.collective_rpc.side_effect = RuntimeError("device lost")
+    core.reject_new_requests = False

+class CheckpointStateResponse(BaseModel):
+    state: CheckpointState
+    error: str | None = None
+
+
+_STATE_RESPONSE = {"model": CheckpointStateResponse}
+
+
+def _state_response(
+    state: CheckpointState, error: str | None, status_code: HTTPStatus
+) -> JSONResponse:
+    content = CheckpointStateResponse(state=state, error=error)
+    return JSONResponse(
+        content=content.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True),
+        status_code=status_code.value,
+    )
+
+
+@router.post(
+    "/checkpoint/prepare",
+    responses={
+        HTTPStatus.OK.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+        HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+    },
+)
+async def checkpoint_prepare(raw_request: Request, mode: PauseMode = "wait"):
+    """Drain with `mode` and release what a checkpoint must not contain.
+    Returns once started; poll /checkpoint/status. Repeating is a no-op."""
+    client = engine_client(raw_request)
+    state, error = await client.checkpoint_state()
+    if state == CheckpointState.RUNNING:
+        if refusal := await client.checkpoint_prepare(mode):
+            return _state_response(state, refusal, HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST)
+        state, error = await client.checkpoint_state()
+    elif state in (CheckpointState.RESTORING, CheckpointState.FAILED):
+        return _state_response(state, error, HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST)
+    return _state_response(state, error, HTTPStatus.OK)
+
+
+@router.post(
+    "/checkpoint/restore",
+    responses={
+        HTTPStatus.OK.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+        HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+    },
+)
+async def checkpoint_restore(raw_request: Request):
+    """Bring back what preparing released and serve. Orchestrators may
+    redeliver, so a restore in progress or done returns 200."""
+    client = engine_client(raw_request)
+    state, error = await client.checkpoint_state()
+    if state in (CheckpointState.PREPARING, CheckpointState.FAILED):
+        return _state_response(state, error, HTTPStatus.BAD_REQUEST)
+    if state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:
+        await client.checkpoint_restore()
+        state, error = await client.checkpoint_state()
+    return _state_response(state, error, HTTPStatus.OK)
+
+
+@router.get(
+    "/checkpoint/status",
+    responses={
+        HTTPStatus.OK.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+        HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+        HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE.value: _STATE_RESPONSE,
+    },
+)
+async def checkpoint_status(raw_request: Request):
+    # Polled by orchestrators: 200 once prepared (safe to capture), 503 until
+    # then, 500 after a failure.
+    state, error = await engine_client(raw_request).checkpoint_state()
+    if state == CheckpointState.PREPARED:
+        status_code = HTTPStatus.OK
+    elif state == CheckpointState.FAILED:
+        status_code = HTTPStatus.INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR
+    else:
+        status_code = HTTPStatus.SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE
+    return _state_response(state, error, status_code)
+
+
+def attach_router(app: FastAPI):
+    app.include_router(router)

inline_comments.body: the multi-port DP supervisor treats a 503 here as a failed child and shuts down all children. can we keep checkpoint preparation from triggering that?
check_health() deliberately succeeds for retired elastic-EP ranks, but this RPC then hits their exited engine and turns the intended 200 into a 500. can we preserve that case?

Good catch, thanks. Fixed in 9c6b815da1 by reverting `/health` to upstream: it stays a liveness check, so a prepared or resuming engine reports 200 like a sleeping one, and the supervisor no longer sees a failed child. New requests still get the retryable `engine_paused` error until resume.
Right, the extra RPC broke the retired-rank case. Same fix in 9c6b815da1: `/health` is back to upstream, so retired elastic-EP ranks get 200 again and `/health` makes no checkpoint call.
